headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: EMQX’s broad egress and IoT data handling can expose content if nuwa-skill consumes shared outputs; other risks are limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, if EMQX outputs are manually copied or routed into nuwa-skill, attacker-controlled content could influence downstream interpretation. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, but the pathway is not default from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF EMQX outputs are copied into nuwa-skill prompts or files
IF nuwa-skill treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoff between the two tools
Add a provenance header to any transferred text
Review imported content before execution
Use separate workspaces for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. If EMQX data is forwarded into nuwa-skill’s context or outputs, sensitive IoT content can leave the original boundary. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF EMQX ingests sensitive IoT payloads
IF nuwa-skill receives those payloads in prompts, files, or outputs
IF the allowlist permits the destination used by nuwa-skill
mitigations: Strip identifiers from IoT payloads before transfer
Restrict nuwa-skill egress allowlist to approved domains
Keep separate storage locations for each agent
Log every cross-agent transfer for review

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and no write surfaces are documented. That means overlap is mainly network-side, not a proven shared mutable resource. Without evidence of shared writes or locking issues, conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external service
IF a shared mutable resource is added later without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials
Separate outbound destinations by agent
Document ownership of each mutable resource
Add a simple lock or queue for shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: EMQX can emit IoT-derived outputs, and nuwa-skill may consume those outputs for research workflows. If nuwa-skill treats EMQX output as authoritative, errors can cascade into reports or actions. The profiles do not show verification steps, so the interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill uses EMQX output as source material
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted
mitigations: Require a verification step before reuse
Mark EMQX output as untrusted by default
Limit downstream actions to drafts only
Spot-check a sample of transferred facts

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad egress, while nuwa-skill is verified but its residency and retention controls are undocumented. If regulated IoT data crosses into nuwa-skill’s environment, retention or residency mismatches could occur. Because the profiles lack explicit compliance claims, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is transferred from EMQX to nuwa-skill
IF nuwa-skill stores or logs that data under different retention rules
mitigations: Classify IoT data before transfer
Avoid sending regulated fields to nuwa-skill
Document retention for both agents
Delete transferred artifacts after use
